name: successful updates preserve ordinary per-user balances
input: an add then a sufficient subtraction
test:
accounts = CreditAccounts()
accounts.add('carol', 14)
assert accounts.get_balance('carol') == 14
accounts.add('dave', 12)
accounts.subtract('dave', 5)
assert accounts.get_balance('dave') == 7

name: an insufficient subtraction is sticky until a success for that user
input: failed withdrawals followed by add and zero-amount success
test:
accounts = CreditAccounts()
accounts.add('erin', 4)
accounts.subtract('erin', 9)
assert accounts.get_balance('erin') is None
accounts.add('erin', 3)
assert accounts.get_balance('erin') == 7
accounts.subtract('erin', 0)
assert accounts.get_balance('erin') == 7

name: failure and recovery are scoped to each user
input: one failed user and one independent successful user
test:
accounts = CreditAccounts()
accounts.add('gina', 9)
accounts.subtract('gina', 4)
accounts.subtract('gina', 8)
assert accounts.get_balance('gina') is None
accounts.add('hank', 2)
assert accounts.get_balance('hank') == 2
accounts.add('gina', 3)
assert accounts.get_balance('gina') == 8
assert accounts.get_balance('hank') == 2

name: unseen accounts read as zero and a zero add is a successful update
input: a missing account and a zero-credit account
test:
accounts = CreditAccounts()
assert accounts.get_balance('missing') == 0
accounts.add('frank', 0)
assert accounts.get_balance('frank') == 0
accounts.subtract('frank', 2)
assert accounts.get_balance('frank') is None
